slides.text: Your state isn’t in your function 🗄️
slides.say: Your component function runs from scratch every render. So where does use state keep its value?

slides.text: React holds the state, not your component. It keeps a list of Hook data for each component.
slides.say: The state is held inside React. For every component on screen, React keeps a list of its Hook data.
Simplified: each component’s fiber carries its Hooks, in call order.

steps.say: On each render, the first Hook call reads slot one, the second reads slot two, and so on.

slides.text: That’s why order must never change, and why state is tied to a position in the tree.
slides.say: That is why Hooks must be called in the same order every render, and why state belongs to a component’s position in the tree. This picture is simplified.
